headline: High-risk data leakage and compliance exposure: aci’s broad egress and CRM/email data can feed social-auto-upload’s upload pipeline, while shared mutable resources are limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest and emit content through MCP/direct function calls, and social-auto-upload consumes local media/account inputs via CLI. No shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is only plausible if an operator manually bridges outputs into upload inputs or captions.
conditions: IF an operator copies aci-generated text into social-auto-upload captions or metadata
IF a shared MCP or clipboard bridge is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not paste aci outputs into upload captions without review
Disable any shared clipboard or shared MCP bridge
Use a human approval step for all generated post text

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; social-auto-upload handles video/image/account data and also has broad egress. The pair does not document a shared filesystem, but if aci outputs sensitive customer content into upload metadata or logs, leakage can occur in default operator workflows.
conditions: IF aci-generated text includes customer or CRM content and is reused in social-auto-upload metadata
IF either agent logs sensitive inputs to a shared external service
mitigations: Strip customer identifiers before reuse
Review captions and descriptions for secrets before upload
Separate credentials and accounts per agent
Turn off verbose logging where possible

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci supports multiple instances and broad API calls, while social-auto-upload explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. There is no documented overlapping write surface, so direct capability conflict is limited unless an external orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable resource.
conditions: IF both agents are granted the same mutable external API account or shared CRM record
IF an orchestrator adds shared write access not present in the profiles
mitigations: Assign separate API accounts
Avoid concurrent edits to the same record
Serialize writes through one operator
Use per-agent queues for mutable tasks

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/research outputs that social-auto-upload could reuse as post text or upload metadata. social-auto-upload is an action-taking uploader, so if its inputs are treated as authoritative without verification, mistakes or hallucinated facts can cascade into public posts or account actions.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload uses aci-generated copy or facts without human verification
IF aci output is mapped directly into upload descriptions or titles
mitigations: Require human review before publishing
Add a fact-check step for aci outputs
Limit aci to drafting only
Use templates that separate facts from promotional text

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles email, CRM, support, and calendar data, while social-auto-upload handles account-linked media and uploads to external platforms. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible if regulated customer data is repurposed into social uploads or stored under different policies.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from aci is copied into social-auto-upload artifacts
IF the two agents retain the same data class under different retention or residency policies
mitigations: Do not move regulated data into upload assets
Document retention for each agent separately
Use redaction before cross-agent transfer
Confirm platform-specific privacy settings before publishing
